# The moments of truth

The spine every journey is hung on. A moment is where a person decides whether to trust, continue or leave: each has the question they are silently asking, the promise the product must keep, how it fails, and the trials that probe it.

| Id | Moment | Side | The question | The promise | How it fails | Surface | Trials |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| M01 | **La vitrine** (The shopfront) | client | Is this the right place, and is it for me? | Five seconds, one glance: where, how much, can I come soon, is it good. | A beautiful hero that answers none of the four; or one that takes six seconds to appear. | / — first viewport | rue, pouce |
| M02 | **La preuve** (The proof) | client | Are they actually good, and who are they? | Real work by real people, and prices that do not need a sentence of explanation. | Stock-looking imagery, initials instead of faces, a menu that hides the price. | / — #coupes, #preuve, #barbiers, #carte | atelier |
| M03 | **Le choix du barbier** (Choosing the person) | client | Who will hold the clippers? | “Anyone” is a respectable answer; a named barber is one tap, with their next free time beside the name. | A forced choice, or a barber presented as a label instead of a person. | booking sheet › Avec qui ? | chrono |
| M04 | **Le créneau** (The slot) | client | When can I come, really? | The earliest slot is one tap; the calendar tells the truth, including when the shop is closed. | A slot offered “today” at 23:00; a calendar with no counts; a spinner. | booking sheet › Quand ? | chrono, nuit |
| M05 | **Les coordonnées** (The details) | client | What do you want from me, and why? | Two required fields, everything else labelled optional, privacy said in one sentence; nothing typed is ever lost. | The keyboard hides the button; an interruption wipes the form; a name with an apostrophe is rejected. | booking sheet › À ton nom | clavier, tram |
| M06 | **La garantie** (The guarantee) | client | What if I cannot come? | The deposit is explained once, in words, before the button, with the cancellation rule beside it. | A deposit discovered at the payment step; a rule that sounds like a penalty. | booking sheet › deposit line, payment | chrono |
| M07 | **La confirmation** (The confirmation) | client | Is it really done, and where do I put it? | Day, hour, barber, address in words; a way to keep it (calendar, SMS); a way to move it without calling. | A thank-you with no details; a dead end. | booking sheet › C’est réservé | chrono |
| M08 | **La veille** (The day before) | client | Something came up. Can I move it without calling? | The SMS link opens one page where the appointment can be moved or cancelled in two taps. | A login wall; a phone number nobody answers. | /r/:token | ancien |
| M09 | **La porte** (The door) | client | Where exactly, and are they open now? | Open or closed, said once, near the address; a directions button; a walk-in wait if there is one. | Hours in a graphic; the open status three scrolls down. | / — #venir, menu | rue |
| M10 | **Le fauteuil** (The chair) | staff | Who is next, and what did he have last time? | The next client, the last cut’s note and two big status buttons, on one screen, readable with wet hands. | A list to scan; a menu to open; small targets; money on show. | /comptoir — Mon espace | mains |
| M11 | **La caisse** (The till) | staff | How much, how does he pay, what about the tip? | Checkout in under thirty seconds, deposits and memberships already deducted, no mis-tap on money. | A secondary action the size of a text link; a modal stacked on a modal. | /comptoir/caisse | mains |
| M12 | **La prochaine** (The next one) | client | Same time in three weeks? | At the chair, the next appointment at his own rhythm is three slots and one tap — the single biggest driver of loyalty. | He leaves without booking and forgets for six weeks. | till confirmation; “Comme la dernière fois ?” | chrono |
| M13 | **Le retour** (The return) | client | Is it time again? Can I just repeat? | Opening the sheet greets him by name and offers last time’s cut with last time’s barber. | He starts from zero, as a stranger, on his own phone. | booking sheet › Bon retour | chrono |
| M14 | **La sortie** (The exit) | client | I want out. Will they let me? | Cancel a membership or erase his data from a footer link, without an account, as easily as he joined. | A maze; a form that asks him to justify himself. | /resilier, /abo/:token, footer | ancien |
| S01 | **L’ouverture** (Opening) | staff | What does today look like? | The day’s agenda, the chairs, today’s walk-in wait and the cash drawer state, in one glance. | A dashboard that needs reading. | /comptoir — Agenda | mains |
| S02 | **Le coup de feu** (The rush) | staff | Who is here, who is late, who is free? | Status changes are one tap, a walk-in is two, and nothing blocks the next action. | A confirmation dialog for a reversible action; a spinner on a tap. | /comptoir — Agenda, Passage | mains |
| S03 | **La clôture** (Closing) | staff | Does the drawer match, and is it sealed? | Count by notes and coins, one seal, a number the accountant can trust. | A number nobody can explain. | /comptoir/caisse/cloture | mains |
| S04 | **Le soir** (The evening numbers) | staff | Is the month on track, and are my barbers paid fairly? | One answer in five seconds; the proof one tap behind it. | Twelve tiles and no verdict. | /comptoir — Pilotage | mains |
